essence: Descent of the scripture told in due course.
Siddhas point, gurus set forth; five divine names.
Nine teachers study the nine-crore expanse from the crore-fund.
Quarters from crores; halves to Dakṣa's and Saṃvarta's lines.
Diminishing shares to the lines; last sixteenth unnamed.
Seventeen fragments: Siṃha, Garuḍa, Vāsuki settled.
Epic descent: Rāvaṇa, Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa onward by guru-disciple rule.
Nineteen fragments, each eightfold, by stated division.
Text-division catalogue; threefold, three toward the goddesses.
Goddesses in expansive order; the ninth quarter uncounted.
Chain: Rāma → Lakṣmaṇa → Siddhas → Dānavas → Guhyakas → Yogins → kings.
Lapse through time; Śrīkaṇṭha-commanded re-descent of the Siddhas.
Three sons skilled in nonduality, duality, duality-nonduality.
Son-line born; daughter-line renowned as Ardhatryambaka.
Gathered lineage-rasa flows as this Tantrāloka in all rasas.
What is worth taking from the descent stands determined.

rasa.dominant: vīra with adbhuta weight (lineage pride; marvel of descent)
rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (the tradition's onward drive) steadied into dhṛti
rasa.justification: The ahnika drives forward — studied, divided, descended, lapsed, restored, housed — and each drive lands; wonder at the sheer scale (crores, kings, maṭhikās) crowns the pride, and the work's own flowing (v15) turns energy into rest.

sections.SUMMARY: The scripture's descent, told in due course. Siddhas point it out, gurus set it forth: Bhairava, Bhairavī Goddess, Svacchanda, Lākula—Aṇurāṭ. Gahaneśa—Abjaja and Śakra study the nine-crore-expanse from the nine, out of the crore-fund. Quarters go out from each crore: halves to Dakṣa's and Saṃvarta's lines, quarters to Vāmana's, half-quarters to Bhārgava, sixteenths to Bali and one other; half to Siṃha, two shares to Garuḍa, a quarter to Vāsuki — seventeen fragments. Heaven's half Rāvaṇa takes, Rāma takes half, and from Vibhīṣaṇa onward it passes by guru-disciple rule. Nineteen fragments, each eightfold, by stated division: quarters, root-extracts, Greater-Uttara, Kalpa, saṃhitā-kalpa and the pervader — threefold, three. The goddesses stand forth in expansive order, uncounted in the undifferentiated ninth quarter. Rāma to Lakṣmaṇa to Siddhas to Dānavas to Guhyakas to Yogins to kings — then lapse through time, and by Śrīkaṇṭha's command the Siddhas descend: Tryambaka, Āmardaka, renowned Śrīnātha, skilled in nonduality, duality, duality-nonduality. The first's line is born, the second through daughter-succession — renowned Ardhatryambaka; four-and-a-half disciple-spread maṭhikās, hundred-branched. The gathered essence-juice of the stream flows as this Tantrāloka in all rasas. What is worth taking from the descent stands now determined.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes the scripture's earthly charter: divine telling, studied expanse, divided transmission through gods, demons, birds, serpents, and kings; lapse and commanded re-descent through three mind-sons parceling one teaching by competence; son-line and daughter-line housed in maṭhikās — closing with the work itself as the stream's gathered rasa, and judgment on what to take.
sections.KEY TERMS: āyāti (descent/arrival of scripture); siddha-guru (double telling); koṭi (crore-fund of verses); pāda (quarter-share); khaṇḍa (fragment: seventeen, then nineteen, each eightfold); mūloddhāra (root-extract); bṛhaduttara (Greater-Uttara); kalpa and saṃhitākalpa (text-divisions); vyāpaka (pervader); navama pada (ninth quarter, undifferentiated); bhraṣṭa (what lapsed); śrīkaṇṭhanātha (Śrīkaṇṭha commander); tryambaka-āmardaka-śrīnātha (three mind-sons: advaya, dvaya, dvayādvaya); duhitṛkrama (daughter-succession); ardhatryambaka (renowned daughter-line); maṭhikā (monastic seat, four-and-a-half); śataśākha (hundred-branching); rasa-āhṛti (gathered essence-juice); syandate (the work flows).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Āhnika 36 is the Tantraloka's transmission-history (āgama-avatāra) before the closing determinations: the pendant to the opening's means (a01) and the finale's entry (a34). Cross-links: Durvāsas-Śrīkaṇṭha origin story (lore); Mālinīvijaya (three samāveśas behind the three sons' competencies); Tantrasara's guru-line passages; a34 (the stream's rasa-yield as the work's self-description).
sections.EXPLANATION: The ahnika runs: (1) topic — descent told in course; first divine roster; (2–3) study of the nine-crore expanse and first quarter-division; (4–5) diminishing shares to the lines, seventeen fragments; (6–7) epic descent (Rāvaṇa, Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa) and nineteen-by-eight fragmentation; (8–9) text-division catalogue and goddess exposition with uncounted ninth; (10–11) human chain to kings, lapse, Śrīkaṇṭha-commanded re-descent; (12–13) three sons and their competencies, son-line and daughter-line (Ardhatryambaka); (14) four-and-a-half maṭhikās hundred-branched; (15–16) the gathered rasa flowing as this work, and judgment on what to take.
